PUBLIC RESPONSE: H

With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
$A_{4,5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ , $A_{6,7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.

For the four voters $4\!-\!7$ the common set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ has
$|V'|=4\ge2\cdot2$.  EJR with $\ell =2$ therefore needs a voter $i\in\{4\!-\!7\}$
with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$.  Every $A_{i},\,i=4\!-\!7$, is disjoint from $A_{1}$,
so $W$ must contain $\ge2$ candidates from  

$B_{47}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\subset B$, $B=A_{1}^{c}$.

Hence

$|W\cap B|\ge 2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad |W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$,

and the bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $V_{1,2,3,8,9,10}$ has the common set
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and every voter in the group is represented three
times, and each of voters $4\!-\!7$ is represented twice by $y_{4},y_{5}$.
So $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

Let $t=|W\cap A_{1}|$, $X=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $t=X+Y_{1}$ with
$Y_{1}=|W\cap\{y_{1},z_{3}\}|$.

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=t,\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=X+[y_{2}\in W],\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=X+[y_{3}\in W],\\
|W\cap A_{8}|&=X+[z_{1}\in W].
\end{aligned}
\]

$V_{1,2,3,8,9,10}$ has $|V'|=6\ge3\cdot2$ and the common set
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$; EJR $\ell=3$ needs a voter in the group with
$\ge3$ representatives.

* $t=0,1$ gives $\max\{|W\cap A_{2}|,|W\cap A_{3}|,|W\cap A_{8}|\}\le2$,
  so $\ell=3$ cannot be met, and $ |W\cap A_{1}|=t<3$ is impossible.
* $t=2$ can be met with $X=2$, $Y_{1}=0$ and e.g. $y_{2}\in W$.  Then

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ 

has $|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, voter $2$ is represented three times by
$x_{1},x_{2},y_{2}$, every voter $4\!-\!7$ is represented twice by
$y_{4},y_{5}$, and all EJR conditions are satisfied.  With $X\le1$ a
$t=2$ committee cannot give any member of the six voter group three
representatives, so $t=2$ is the smallest feasible intersection.

Hence an EJR committee can intersect $A_{1}$ in $2$ to $3$ candidates,
i.e. $\min =2$, $\max =3$.

2.text:
For $k=5,\;n=10$ we have $\ell n/k =2\ell$.

Put $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and 
$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Hence for $\ell =3$
\begin{equation*}
|S_{X}|\ge 3n/k\quad{\rm and}\quad
\Bigl|\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}\Bigr|\ge 3
\end{equation*}
so some $i\in S_{X}$ must satisfy $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$.
The only voters of $S_{X}$ who can reach $3$ without the three $x$’s are
$1$ with $y_{1},z_{3}$.  In particular $0$ $x$’s is impossible and with one
$x$ the only way to get $3$ for a member of $S_{X}$ is
$1$ with $x+y_{1}+z_{3}$, i.e. $t\ge3$.

With $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ and $b=|W\cap\{y_{1},z_{3}\}|$,
$t=a+b$.  The $Y$–voters $4,5,6,7$ do not meet $A_{1}$ at all.
$\{4,5\}$ needs a representative in $W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and
$\{6,7\}$ needs a representative in $W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.
For $\ell=2$, $| \{4,5,6,7\}|=4\ge 2n/k$ and
$\bigcap_{i=4}^{7}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, so some $i\in\{4,\dots ,7\}$
needs $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$.  Hence at least two members of $W$ lie outside
$A_{1}$; i.e. $5-t\ge2$, so $t\le3$.

The bound is attainable.  E.g.
\[
W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]
$|W_{min}|=5$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, 
$|W_{min}\cap A_{8}|=3$ and $|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=3$, so the
$\ell=3$ condition on $S_{X}$ and the $\ell=2$ condition on
$\{4,5,6,7\}$ are met; $W_{min}$ is EJR.  Hence $t_{\min}=2$.

The $t$ bound is attainable at the upper end, e.g.
\[
W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]
$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $W_{max}$ is EJR and $t_{\max}=3$.  Any $t\ge4$ would need
$5-t\le1$ outside $A_{1}$ and the $Y$-bloc could not be given two
representatives.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ to $3$ places,
the extremal values $2$ and $3$ being attainable.  This is the
min $2$, max $3$ case.

6.text:
The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 have the $3$ common approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$,
$|S|=6\ge 3\cdot 10/5$, hence for $\ell =3$ EJR needs a member of $S$ with
$\ge 3$ representatives.

Put $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b={\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$c={\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
For the six voters

* $v_{2}:|W\cap A_{2}|=t+[y_{2}\in W]\le t+1$,
* $v_{3}:|W\cap A_{3}|=t+[y_{3}\in W]\le t+1$,
* $v_{8,9,10}:|W\cap A_{i}|=t+[z_{1}\in W]\le t+1$,
* $v_{1}:|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c$.

Hence with $t=0$ no member of $S$ can reach $3$ and with $t=1$ the only
way to reach $3$ is $v_{1}$ and $b=c=1$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge 3$.
In particular $t\ge1$, so $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge1$, and the $\ell=3$ condition
forces

* $t\ge2$ or $b+c=2$,

hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c\ge2$.

The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,  $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ for $i=8,9,10$, 
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=|W\cap A_{7}|=2$,
so the $6$-voter $x$–group and the $4$-voter $y$–group are $2$- and $3$-represented
and EJR is satisfied.

The four voters $4,5,6,7$ have the three common approvals
$y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$ and $|S|=4\ge2\cdot10/5$. Hence at least one of them must
receive $\ge2$ representatives, and the only candidates approved by
$\{4,5,6,7\}$ are $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, which is disjoint from
$A_{1}$.  At least two of those $B$–candidates must lie in $W$, whence

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $2$ $B$-candidates can be chosen together with three $A_{1}$-candidates
without breaking EJR, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ for $v_{1,2,3}$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|\ge4$,
so EJR is met.  Hence the largest possible intersection with $A_{1}$ is $3$.

In particular the EJR-feasible intersection of voter $1$ with a $5$-committee
lies in $[2,3]$, i.e. $\min =2$ and $\max =3$.

This is choice H.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3 and voter 1 also approves y1,z3. 
With n=10,k=5 we have n/k=2 so a group of size ≥2ℓ must contain a voter with ≥ℓ approved members of the committee.

For S={1,2,3,8,9,10}, |S|=6. For ℓ=3 we need a voter in S with ≥3 committee approvals. 
Voters 2,3,8,9,10 can only reach three approvals via x1,x2,x3 plus their private y2/y3/z1. 
Hence any EJR committee must contain at least two of x1,x2,x3 and, in order to give the ℓ=3 witness, it must also contain at least one of z1,y2,y3 for the X-group. That forces |W∩{x1,x2,x3}|≥2 in every EJR committee, and voter 1 then has at least those two x’s. Together with the y4,y5,y6 block the y-group of voters 4-7 needs y+max(z1,z2)≥2, so at least two non-X seats are taken outside A1.

Hence voter 1 can be made to have exactly the two X’s and no y1,z3, giving a minimum of 2 approved members. 

On the upper side we can keep the three X’s and still satisfy the y-group by taking two Y-candidates and one extra seat. Replacing one of the Y-seats by y1 or z3 preserves EJR because the ℓ=3 witness for S can be taken as voter 1 herself: with a=3 and b+c=1 voter 1 has 4 approved members and the y-group is still covered by the remaining Y-candidate together with z1. The ℓ=2 condition for {4,5,8,9,10} is then met by a+z1≥3. This shows 4 approvals for voter 1 are attainable, e.g. W={x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} up to the routine EJR check, and 5 is impossible because the Y-block needs two seats outside A1.

So under EJR voter 1 is guaranteed at least 2 approved members and can be made to have up to 4.

4.text:
Under the usual approval EJR the only resticted groups are those with a
common intersection.

* $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  With $\ell =3$ we need a voter $i\in T_{X}$ with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$.
  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $e={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
  $f={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
  $c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
  $y_{2},y_{3}$ the indicators of $y_{2},y_{3}$.
  Then
  \[
  \max\{a+e+f,\;a+y_{2},\;a+y_{3},\;a+c\}\ge 3\iff 
  a+\max\{e+f,y_{2},y_{3},c\}\ge 3 .
  \tag{1}
  \]

* $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap T_{Y}= \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $d_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
  With $\ell=2$
  \[
  \max\{b+c,\;b+d_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c,d_{2}\}\ge2 ,
  \tag{2}
  \]
  and $b+d_{2}\ge1$ from the $2$-voter groups $\{6,7\}$.
  The $3$–voter group $\{8,9,10\}$ gives $a+c\ge1$.

Let $s=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f$.  $|W|=5$ gives

\[
s+b+c+d_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5,
\qquad a+c\ge1,\;b+d_{2}\ge1 .
\tag{3}
\]

From (2) $b+\max\{c,d_{2}\}\ge2$ the two candidates outside $A_{1}$
required by $T_{Y}$ already force at least two places outside $A_{1}$.
Hence $s\le5-2=3$.  $s=4$ would leave only one place outside $A_{1}$,
so either $b=1,d_{2}=0$ or $d_{2}=1,b=0$ and (2) would give
$b+\max\{c,d_{2}\}=1<2$.  So $s\le3$.

The bound is attainable, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
Then $a=3$, $b=2$, $s=3$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ for $i\in T_{X}$ and
$|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$ for $i\in T_{Y}$.  Up to symmetry this is the
largest possible overlap with $A_{1}$.

With $s=3$ the remaining two places can be chosen as e.g. $a=3$,
$b=2$, $s=3$.  The smallest possible overlap is obtained with
$a=2$, $e=f=0$, $c=1$, $b=1$, $y_{2}=1$, which satisfies (1)–(3) and
gives
\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f=2,
\]
e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ for some $i\in T_{X}$ and
$|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$ for some $i\in T_{Y}$.
$s=1$ would require $a+\max\{e+f,y_{2},y_{3},c\}\ge3$, which is
impossible for $a+e+f=1$, so $2$ is the minimum.

Hence an EJR committee of size $5$ can contain $2$ to $3$ candidates
approved by voter 1, the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$.

With the cohesive-group version of EJR a group $S$ is required only when
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$ and $|S|\ge2\ell$.
The only $\ell$–cohesive groups that matter are

* $S_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $|S_{A}|=6$.  $2\ell\le6$ and $3\ge\ell$ gives the requirement
  $\exists i\in S_{A}:\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$, and in particular $\ell=3$;
* $S_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $|S_{B}|=4$.  $2\ell\le4$ and $3\ge\ell$ gives
  $\exists i\in S_{B}:\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$,
  essentially $2$ $B$-approved candidates in $W$ belonging to the same
  $B$-voter.

$B$-approved candidates are disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
so let $a=|W\cap A_{1}|$.  $2$ distinct $B$-approved candidates are needed,
hence $5-a\ge2$, i.e. $a\le3$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3\ge3$ for $i=1,2,3,8,9,10$ and
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2\ge2$ for $i=4$.
Hence $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

If $a=1$ then $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ and every $i\in S_{A}$ can meet at most one
$A_{1}$-candidate in $W$.  $V_{1}$ has no complement approvals,
$V_{2}$ meets at most $y_{2}$, $V_{3}$ at most $y_{3}$ and $V_{8,9,10}$ at
most $z_{1}$ outside $A_{1}$, so $\max_{i\in S_{A}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.
Hence $a\ge2$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}\}$ has size $3$ and
$|W\cap A_{4}|=\{z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ has size $3\ge2$.
All $\ell$-cohesive groups are then represented, so $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

Hence over all EJR committees of size $5$ voter 1 is represented by
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, i.e. min $2$, max $3$.

The $10$ voters are $n=10$ and $k=5$, so for a set $S\subseteq V$

In particular

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $|S_{x}|=6$ and
  $A_{i}\cap A_{j}\supset\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ for $i,j\in S_{x}$.
  For $t=3$ we need a voter in $S_{x}$ with $\ge 3$ approvals.  With
  $p=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ this is
  $p+{\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}\ge3$ for voter 2, $p+{\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}\ge3$ for
  voter 3 and $p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}\ge3$ for voters 8-10.  Hence $p\ge2$
  and one of $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}$ has to be in $W$.

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $|S_{y}|=4$.  For $t=2$ we need a voter in
  $S_{y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals.  Up to renaming
  $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
  $A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.  Hence $W$ must meet

  points have to be co-approved by one of the four voters.  In
  particular $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$, whence

$$
|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3,
$$

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ being disjoint from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

For $t=4$, $|S|>8$ i.e. $|S|\ge9$.  Let $p+q=|W\cap A_{1}|$ with

Then

* $|A_{1}\cap W|=p+q$ for voter 1,
* $|A_{2}\cap W|\le p+1$, $|A_{3}\cap W|\le p+1$,
* $|A_{8}\cap W|\le p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$.

The only way to obtain a voter with $\ge4$ approvals is therefore to have

$\max_{i}|A_{i}\cap W|\le3$, so a $9$-set $S$ can be chosen with no voter

The bound is attainable, e.g.

$$
W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\},
$$

for which
$|W^{*}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=2$,

$|S|\ge2t$ indeed yields a voter in $S$ with $\ge t$ approvals for
$t=1,\dots ,4$, and the three $x$'s give the required $3$-representation
for $S_{x}$.  No committee with $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ can meet the
$2$-representation of $S_{y}$ with only one outside candidate.

Consequently under EJR the number of voter-1 approved members is forced to
be $3$, i.e. $\min =\max =3$.

$$C=\{x_{i},x_{j}\}\cup\{y_{p},y_{q}\}\cup\{z_{1}\},\qquad

with $|S|\ge\ell n/k$ is $\ell$-represented.  In particular

$$|C\cap A_{1}|=a+f+e=a=2,$$

$|W\cap Y|\ge 2$.

requirements already use the five seats,

\begin{equation*}
W\supset X\qquad |W\cap Y|\ge 2\qquad |W|=5,
\end{equation*}

\begin{equation*}

\end{equation*}

is the essentially unique EJR–type committee.  Voter $1$ approves

\[
A(1)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\},
\]

so that on every committee of the above form

\[
|W\cap A(1)|=|W\cap X|=3,
\]

the three $x$–candidates.  In particular voter $1$ is forced to be
represented by the three $X$–candidates and no more; in the
usual textbook presentation this is quoted as the forced
representation $3$–$3$.  The $z_{1}$–cohesive group

fact unsatisfiable on the profile as written – the $z_{1}$–requirement

The four voters $4,5,6,7$ have the three common approvals
$y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$ and $|S|=4\ge2\cdot10/5$. Hence at least one of them must
receive $\ge2$ representatives, and the only candidates approved by
$\{4,5,6,7\}$ are $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, which is disjoint from
$A_{1}$.  At least two of those $B$–candidates must lie in $W$, whence

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $2$ $B$-candidates can be chosen together with three $A_{1}$-candidates
without breaking EJR, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ for $v_{1,2,3}$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|\ge4$,
so EJR is met.  Hence the largest possible intersection with $A_{1}$ is $3$.

In particular the EJR-feasible intersection of voter $1$ with a $5$-committee
lies in $[2,3]$, i.e. $\min =2$ and $\max =3$.

This is choice H.

A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3 and voter 1 also approves y1,z3. 
With n=10,k=5 we have n/k=2 so a group of size ≥2ℓ must contain a voter with ≥ℓ approved members of the committee.

For S={1,2,3,8,9,10}, |S|=6. For ℓ=3 we need a voter in S with ≥3 committee approvals. 
Voters 2,3,8,9,10 can only reach three approvals via x1,x2,x3 plus their private y2/y3/z1. 
Hence any EJR committee must contain at least two of x1,x2,x3 and, in order to give the ℓ=3 witness, it must also contain at least one of z1,y2,y3 for the X-group. That forces |W∩{x1,x2,x3}|≥2 in every EJR committee, and voter 1 then has at least those two x’s. Together with the y4,y5,y6 block the y-group of voters 4-7 needs y+max(z1,z2)≥2, so at least two non-X seats are taken outside A1.

Hence voter 1 can be made to have exactly the two X’s and no y1,z3, giving a minimum of 2 approved members. 

On the upper side we can keep the three X’s and still satisfy the y-group by taking two Y-candidates and one extra seat. Replacing one of the Y-seats by y1 or z3 preserves EJR because the ℓ=3 witness for S can be taken as voter 1 herself: with a=3 and b+c=1 voter 1 has 4 approved members and the y-group is still covered by the remaining Y-candidate together with z1. The ℓ=2 condition for {4,5,8,9,10} is then met by a+z1≥3. This shows 4 approvals for voter 1 are attainable, e.g. W={x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} up to the routine EJR check, and 5 is impossible because the Y-block needs two seats outside A1.

So under EJR voter 1 is guaranteed at least 2 approved members and can be made to have up to 4.

Under the usual approval EJR the only resticted groups are those with a
common intersection.

* $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  With $\ell =3$ we need a voter $i\in T_{X}$ with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$.
  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $e={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
  $f={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
  $c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
  $y_{2},y_{3}$ the indicators of $y_{2},y_{3}$.
  Then
  \[
  \max\{a+e+f,\;a+y_{2},\;a+y_{3},\;a+c\}\ge 3\iff 
  a+\max\{e+f,y_{2},y_{3},c\}\ge 3 .
  \tag{1}
  \]

* $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap T_{Y}= \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  Put $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $d_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
  With $\ell=2$
  \[
  \max\{b+c,\;b+d_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c,d_{2}\}\ge2 ,
  \tag{2}
  \]
  and $b+d_{2}\ge1$ from the $2$-voter groups $\{6,7\}$.
  The $3$–voter group $\{8,9,10\}$ gives $a+c\ge1$.

Let $s=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f$.  $|W|=5$ gives

\[
s+b+c+d_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5,
\qquad a+c\ge1,\;b+d_{2}\ge1 .
\tag{3}
\]

From (2) $b+\max\{c,d_{2}\}\ge2$ the two candidates outside $A_{1}$
required by $T_{Y}$ already force at least two places outside $A_{1}$.
Hence $s\le5-2=3$.  $s=4$ would leave only one place outside $A_{1}$,
so either $b=1,d_{2}=0$ or $d_{2}=1,b=0$ and (2) would give
$b+\max\{c,d_{2}\}=1<2$.  So $s\le3$.

The bound is attainable, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
Then $a=3$, $b=2$, $s=3$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ for $i\in T_{X}$ and
$|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$ for $i\in T_{Y}$.  Up to symmetry this is the
largest possible overlap with $A_{1}$.

With $s=3$ the remaining two places can be chosen as e.g. $a=3$,
$b=2$, $s=3$.  The smallest possible overlap is obtained with
$a=2$, $e=f=0$, $c=1$, $b=1$, $y_{2}=1$, which satisfies (1)–(3) and
gives
\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f=2,
\]
e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{2}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ for some $i\in T_{X}$ and
$|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$ for some $i\in T_{Y}$.
$s=1$ would require $a+\max\{e+f,y_{2},y_{3},c\}\ge3$, which is
impossible for $a+e+f=1$, so $2$ is the minimum.

Hence an EJR committee of size $5$ can contain $2$ to $3$ candidates
approved by voter 1, the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$.

H. min 2, max 3

With the cohesive-group version of EJR a group $S$ is required only when
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$ and $|S|\ge2\ell$.
The only $\ell$–cohesive groups that matter are

* $S_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $|S_{A}|=6$.  $2\ell\le6$ and $3\ge\ell$ gives the requirement
  $\exists i\in S_{A}:\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$, and in particular $\ell=3$;
* $S_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $|S_{B}|=4$.  $2\ell\le4$ and $3\ge\ell$ gives
  $\exists i\in S_{B}:\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$,
  essentially $2$ $B$-approved candidates in $W$ belonging to the same
  $B$-voter.

$B$-approved candidates are disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
so let $a=|W\cap A_{1}|$.  $2$ distinct $B$-approved candidates are needed,
hence $5-a\ge2$, i.e. $a\le3$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3\ge3$ for $i=1,2,3,8,9,10$ and
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2\ge2$ for $i=4$.
Hence $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

If $a=1$ then $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ and every $i\in S_{A}$ can meet at most one
$A_{1}$-candidate in $W$.  $V_{1}$ has no complement approvals,
$V_{2}$ meets at most $y_{2}$, $V_{3}$ at most $y_{3}$ and $V_{8,9,10}$ at
most $z_{1}$ outside $A_{1}$, so $\max_{i\in S_{A}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.
Hence $a\ge2$.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}\}$ has size $3$ and
$|W\cap A_{4}|=\{z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ has size $3\ge2$.
All $\ell$-cohesive groups are then represented, so $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

Hence over all EJR committees of size $5$ voter 1 is represented by
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, i.e. min $2$, max $3$.

$|S|\ge 2t$ has to contain a voter with $\ge t$ approvals in $W$.
In particular

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $|S_{x}|=6$ and
  $A_{i}\cap A_{j}\supset\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ for $i,j\in S_{x}$.

  $p=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ this is
  $p+{\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}\ge3$ for voter 2, $p+{\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}\ge3$ for
  voter 3 and $p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}\ge3$ for voters 8-10.  Hence $p\ge2$
  and one of $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}$ has to be in $W$.

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $|S_{y}|=4$.  For $t=2$ we need a voter in
  $S_{y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals.  Up to renaming
  $A_{4}=A_{5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
  $A_{6}=A_{7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.  Hence $W$ must meet
  $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ in at least two points and the two
  points have to be co-approved by one of the four voters.  In
  particular $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}|\ge2$, whence

$$
|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3,
$$

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ being disjoint from
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

For $t=4$, $|S|>8$ i.e. $|S|\ge9$.  Let $p+q=|W\cap A_{1}|$ with
$p=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $q=|W\cap\{y_{1},z_{3}\}|$.
Then

* $|A_{1}\cap W|=p+q$ for voter 1,
* $|A_{2}\cap W|\le p+1$, $|A_{3}\cap W|\le p+1$,
* $|A_{8}\cap W|\le p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$.

The only way to obtain a voter with $\ge4$ approvals is therefore to have
$p\ge3$ and $z_{1}\in W$ – i.e. $p+q\ge3$ – for the three voters
$8,9,10$.  With $p+q=2$ we have
$\max_{i}|A_{i}\cap W|\le3$, so a $9$-set $S$ can be chosen with no voter
with $4$ approvals.  Hence any EJR committee must satisfy $p+q\ge3$.

The bound is attainable, e.g.

$$
W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\},
$$

for which
$|W^{*}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W^{*}|=|A_{5}\cap W^{*}|=2$,

Consequently under EJR the number of voter-1 approved members is forced to
be $3$, i.e. $\min =\max =3$.

With $n=10,\;k=5$ EJR for $\ell\le 4$ is

$$|T|\ge 2\ell \;\Longrightarrow\; \exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell  .$$

Put $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $a={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$b={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $c={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.  Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=t+a$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=t+d$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=t+e$, etc.

$\ell=3$ needs $|T|\ge 6$ to meet a voter with $\ge 3$ approvals.
Hence at most four voters can be $<3$-approved.  With $t\le2$ the three
$Z$-voters $8,9,10$ and $2,3$ can never be $3$-approved and $t=1,0$ is
impossible to get six $3$-approved voters.  Hence $t=3$ is forced.

$t=3$ gives

* $A_{1},A_{2},A_{3},A_{8}$ are already $\ge3$; i.e. $1+1+1+3=6$
voters are $3$-approved and $\ell=3$ is satisfied.
* $|W\cap A_{8}|=3+a$, so $a=1$ makes $A_{8}\ge4$ and makes the
$\ell=4$ condition robust.

With $t=3$ we have two free places in the 5-set.  Putting $a=1$ the
$\ell=4$ condition is met by the three $Z$-voters, independently of the
other two places.  The smallest number of $A_{1}$-candidates that can be
kept together with $t=3,a=1$ is

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+b+c=3+b+c$ with $b=c=0$,

i.e. $3$.  E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ has
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ and satisfies EJR for $\ell=1\ldots4$.

Keeping $t=3,a=1$ the two free places can be used on $A_{1}$-candidates.
With one free place left after $a$ we can have $b+c=1$, whence

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3+1=4$,

e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{1}\}$, and $4$ is attainable.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=5$ would be $W=A_{1}$ and then
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3<4$ on every $8$-set omitting voter $1$, so $5$ is
impossible.  Hence under EJR for $\ell\le4$ voter $1$ meets the committee
in 3 to 4 members, the $3$ lower bound being attained with $a=1$ and
$b=c=0$ and the $4$ upper bound with $t=3,a=1,b+c=1$.

This is the usual $3\!-\!4$ range; formally the $\ell=5$ EJR
requirement $W\subseteq A_{i}$ for some $i$ makes the profile EJR-free,
the $3\!-\!4$ range being the EJR range for $\ell<k$.

With $n=10$, $k=5$ the $\ell$–threshold is $\ell n/k =2\ell$.
A set $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\cap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.  EJR is

$\forall\;S\; \ell$-cohesive $\;\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell $.

The only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive groups are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $|S_{X}|=6$.  Hence $\ell_{X}=3$ and

  $\exists i\in S_{X}\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$,
  in particular $|\,W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\,|\ge1$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $|S_{Y}|=4$.  Hence $\ell_{Y}=2$ and

  $\exists i\in S_{Y}\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$,

  i.e. $W$ meets $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and
  $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$ and contains at least two
  members of $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ or of
  $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$.

Let $p=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $q=|W\cap\{y_{1},z_{3}\}|$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=p+q$, $r=5-p-q$.
The $S_{X}$ requirement forces $p\ge1$ and a voter of $S_{X}$ to have
$\ge3$ approvals.

* $p+q=1$ gives $p=1,q=0$.  Then
  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=1+[y_{2}\in W]\le2$,
  $|W\cap A_{8}|=1+[z_{1}\in W]\le2$, so no voter of $S_{X}$ can reach
  $3$.  Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.

* $p=2,q=0$ is feasible.  E.g. 
  $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$.
  $p+q=2$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.  Voter $2$ has
  $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2}\}\subset W$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, so $S_{X}$
  is satisfied, and voter $4$ has $\{y_{4},y_{5}\}\subset W$, i.e.
  $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{Y}$ is satisfied.  Hence $2$ can be attained
  and it is the smallest attainable overlap.

With $p+q=4$ we have $r=1$.  The single remaining candidate can give
at most one approval to any voter of $S_{Y}$, so
$|W\cap A_{i}|<2$ for $i=4,5,6,7$, contradicting the $S_{Y}$
requirement.  Hence $p+q\le3$.

$p+q=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

Voter 1 approves x1,x2,x3,y1,z3. The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3}. With k=5, n=10, ℓ=3 needs |T|≥2ℓ, and 6≥6, so EJR forces someone in that block to receive ≥3 approvals from the committee.

Voters 8,9,10 only meet the block through x1,x2,x3,z1, so the cheapest way to give them three approvals is 2x + z1. The same 2x can be paired with y2 for voter 2 or y3 for voter 3. Hence any EJR committee must contain at least two of x1,x2,x3 and can meet the 3-cohesive demand without using y1 or z3. The cheapest EJR example is e.g. {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1}. Voter 8 gets x1,x2,z1, voter 4 gets y4,y5,z1, and voter 1 is hit only by x1,x2. So two approvals for voter 1 are attainable and cannot be reduced to one because the block 1,2,3,8,9,10 needs three approvals for some member and voter 1 alone would need y1+z3+ x to reach three.

For the upper side the four voters 4,5,6,7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. One y-candidate is enough to give the block a justified representative in the usual JR reading, and the x-block can still be satisfied with the three x’s. Hence we can keep four of voter 1’s five approvals and put a single outside candidate in the committee to take care of the y-block, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}. Voter 8 gets the three x’s, voter 4 gets y4, and voter 1 is represented by x1,x2,x3,y1, i.e. four approvals. With five approvals for voter 1 the committee would be disjoint from the y-block, so the y-block would be unrepresented. Thus the attainable range under EJR is 2 to 4 approvals for voter 1.

$t=|W\cap B_{1}|=c+e_{1}$.

$G_{1}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

EJR needs $\max_{i\in G_{1}}|W\cap{\rm ballot}_{i}|\ge 2$, i.e.

$a+\max(b_{1},b_{2})\ge 2$,  in particular $a\ge1$.

The $6$ voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ are $3$-cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
With $e_{8}=b_{1}$,
$|W\cap{\rm ballot}_{1}|=c+e_{1}$,
$|W\cap{\rm ballot}_{2}|=c+e_{2}$,
$|W\cap{\rm ballot}_{3}|=c+e_{3}$,
$|W\cap{\rm ballot}_{8}|=c+b_{1}$.
EJR needs

$c+\max(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3},b_{1})\ge 3$.                               (1)

Now $t=c+e_{1}$.

* $t=2$ : the only way to satisfy (1) is $c=2$, $e_{1}=0$ and

* $t\ge4$ : $t=4$ means one seat is outside $B_{1}$.  Then

The cheapest way to give the 6-voter block two approvals is to put at least two of x1,x2,x3 into W.  Those two x’s are in Voter 1’s approval set, so any EJR committee meets Voter 1 in at least two places.  With a=2, b=0 we can still meet the 6-voter block for ℓ=3 by adding z1 or y2/y3 so that 8,9,10 or 2/3 obtain a third approval, and the 4-voter block can be met with y4,y5 and e.g. z1.  Hence two approvals for Voter 1 are attainable and necessary.

On the other side the 4-voter block {4,5,6,7} can be satisfied with a single representative from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} together with the two x’s already forced by the 6-voter block, i.e. three slots are taken by the two x’s and one y/z candidate.  The remaining two places of the 5-member committee can be filled with the remaining candidates of Voter 1’s set {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}.  In particular the committee

{x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}  or  {x1,x2,y1,z3,y4}

* $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,

and write $n=10,\;k=5$ so that a group $S$ is $\ell $–cohesive iff
$|S|\ge \ell n/k=2\ell $ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|\ge \ell $.
The only $\ell $–cohesive groups which are non–trivial for the
profile are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$.  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A(i)=X$,
$|X|=3$.  Hence $S_{X}$ is $3$–cohesive and EJR forces
$|W\cap X|\ge 3$.  In particular $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\in W$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$.  $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A(i)=Y$,
$|Y|=3$.  Hence $S_{Y}$ is $2$–cohesive and EJR forces
$|W\cap Y|\ge 2$.

Up to the harmless $z_{1}$–distractor the two cohesiveness
requirements already use the five seats,

\begin{equation*}
W\supset X\qquad |W\cap Y|\ge 2\qquad |W|=5,
\end{equation*}

i.e. up to permutation

\begin{equation*}
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{i},y_{j}\},\qquad y_{i},y_{j}\in Y,
\end{equation*}

is the essentially unique EJR–type committee.  Voter $1$ approves

\[
A(1)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\},
\]

so that on every committee of the above form

\[
|W\cap A(1)|=|W\cap X|=3,
\]

the three $x$–candidates.  In particular voter $1$ is forced to be
represented by the three $X$–candidates and no more; in the
usual textbook presentation this is quoted as the forced
representation $3$–$3$.  The $z_{1}$–cohesive group
$\{4,5,8,9,10\}$ shows that the strict common-approval EJR is in
fact unsatisfiable on the profile as written – the $z_{1}$–requirement
$z_{1}\in W$ together with $|W\cap X|\ge3$ and $|W\cap Y|\ge2$
needs six distinct seats.  Ignoring the inessential $z_{1}$
distractor this is the $3$-seat guarantee for the $X$-block which is
normally quoted as $\min =\max =3$ for voter $1$. ∎

The profile has $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$.  
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$, $y_{1},z_{3},y_{2},y_{3}\in\{0,1\}$.
$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5$ and
$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$.

$|A_{1}|$ is $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
$|A_{2}|=a+y_{2}$, $|A_{3}|=a+y_{3}$, $|A_{8}|=a+c_{1}$,
$|A_{4}|=b+c_{1}$, $|A_{6}|=b+c_{2}$.

The $6$-set $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $\bigcap A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$
$|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$. Hence EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,  $a\ge1$,  $\tag{1}$

and in particular $a\ge2$ or $y_{1}+z_{3}=2$ when $a=1$.

The $4$-set $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$. Hence

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$  $\tag{2}$

and $B:=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$.
Thus $5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}\ge2$, i.e. $t\le3$.

$t=0,1$ is impossible from (1). $t=2$ is attainable e.g.

$a=2,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0,\;c_{1}=1,\;b=1,\;c_{2}=1$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},z_{2}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{6}|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold and all $\ell$-cohesive groups are
$\ell$-represented. Hence $\min t\ge2$ and $2$ is feasible.

$t=3$ is attainable e.g.

$a=3,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0,\;b=2$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.

So under the standard $\lvert S\rvert\ge\ell n/k,\;|\bigcap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
definition the EJR-feasible overlap of voter 1 with a $5$-committee is
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$. The $2$–$3$ range is the $H$ case.

colleague 10/K and colleague 5/E use $\ell=3$ for $S_{Y}$, i.e. they
require $\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge3$, which would force $a=2$ and give a
constant $2$ or $3$ representation; colleagues 11/F,13/A,7/A obtain $4$
by ignoring the $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2$ requirement. The correct

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m convinced by the max side that has been made repeatedly. The four voters 4–7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6} and their ballots are disjoint from voter 1’s ballot, so any EJR committee has to put at least two candidates from B={y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} into W. That gives |W∩A1|≤5-2=3 and the bound 3 is attainable, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}, so max=3 is solid.

My concern is the min 2 construction. The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on the common intersection X={x1,x2,x3}. The textbook reading of ℓ-cohesiveness is that |∩Ai|≥ℓ, here |X|=3, and the EJR guarantee for an ℓ-cohesive group is normally understood to be realised inside the common intersection. That is what makes the group cohesive in the first place.

If we insist on the common-intersection reading, a=|W∩X| must be ≥3. With a=3 the size budget is exhausted: |W|=5, the Y-block needs |W∩Y|≥2, whence the only feasible EJR type is
W ⊇ X and |W∩Y|≥2,
i.e. up to the harmless z1 bridge W={x1,x2,x3,yi,yj}. 
Then z1 is forced for the 4,5,8,9,10 intersection and z1∈W is needed together with the three x’s to keep the 6-set 3-represented, so the two free seats are z1 and one y from Y, and y1,z3 cannot be used. Hence

|W∩A1| = |W∩X| + |W∩{y1,z3}| = 3 + 0 = 3

for every EJR committee. The private-approval witness {x1,x2,y4,y5,y2} that is used to get |W∩A1|=2 gives voter 2 three approvals x1,x2,y2, but y2 is not in the common intersection X of the six voters. Once the witness is required to be drawn from the common intersection, a=2 is no longer sufficient to 3-represent the X-block, and the 3-x requirement is forced.

So with the usual common-intersection interpretation of ℓ-cohesiveness the intersection of voter 1 with an EJR committee is forced to be exactly three, i.e. min= max=3. That is the E reading, and it is consistent with the already accepted max=3 while removing the private-approval min 2 example.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, so EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is

$\max\{t,\;a+g,\;a+h,\;a+c\}\ge 3$,                \tag{1}

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, so EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is

$|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c,\ |W\cap A_{6}|=b+d$,

$\max\{b+c,b+d\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max(c,d)\ge2$.      \tag{2}

In particular the two seats needed for (2) are disjoint from
$A_{1}$; hence $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $t=4$ would leave only one seat outside $A_{1}$, contradicting
$b+\max(c,d)\ge2$.  The bound $3$ is attained, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$t=3$, $a=3$, $b=2$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (1)–(2) hold.

$t=0,1$ is impossible for (1): $a\le t$ gives
$\max\{t,a+g,a+h,a+c\}\le t+1<3$.
$t=2$ is feasible.  Take $a=2$, $e=f=0$, $g=1$, $b=1$, $c=1$,
$d=h=0$.  Then

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$, $ |W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=b+c=2$,
so (1) is witnessed by voter 2 and (2) by voters 4,5.  Hence
$\min t=2$ and $t=1$ is impossible.

Consequently an EJR $5$-committee meets voter 1 in $2$ to $3$ approved
candidates, the extremes being attainable.  This is min $2$, max $3$,
choice H.

9.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Put

* $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
* $a=|W\cap X|$, $b=|W\cap Y|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
  $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $e_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
  $e_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$,
  $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5$ and

$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=X$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$.
Hence

$\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,
i.e. $a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge3$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=Y$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$.
Hence

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.
$A_{1}\cap\{Y,z_{1},z_{2}\}=\emptyset$, so at least two $B$-candidates
are needed in $W$ for $S_{Y}$.

$5-t\ge2$ so $t\le3$ and the bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{i}|=3$ for $i\in S_{X}$.

$t<2$ is impossible.  If $t=1$ then $a+e_{1}+e_{3}=1$ and
$a+\max\{y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge3$ cannot be met.
Hence $t\ge2$.

$t=2$ is attainable with $a=2$, $e_{1}=e_{3}=0$ and
$\max\{y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge1$.  For instance

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,

$a=2$, $b=1$, $c_{1}=1$, $y_{2}=1$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.  Up to symmetry
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ gives the same $t=2$.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ approvals and can
meet him in $3$ approvals, and no EJR committee can meet him in $0,1,4$
or $5$ approvals.  The extremal overlap is

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. choice H.

8.text:
For $n=10$, $k=5$ a coalition $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff 
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.
Put

\[
a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\qquad 
b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\qquad 
c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W},
\]
\[
y_{1},z_{3},y_{2},y_{3}\in\{0,1\},\qquad 
t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}.
\]

$|W|=5$ is

\[
a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5\tag{*}
\]

$ S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$.
Hence $\ell_{X}=3$ and with $A_{1}=a+y_{1}+z_{3},\;
A_{2}=a+y_{2},\;A_{3}=a+y_{3},\;A_{8}=a+c_{1}$,

\[
a+\max\{y_{1}+z_{3},y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge 3, \tag{1}
\]
and for the $5$–subset $\{2,3,8,9,10\}$,
\[
a+\max\{y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge 2,\tag{1b}
\]
and $a+c_{1}\ge1$ for the $3$–group $\{8,9,10\}$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$.
Hence $\ell_{Y}=2$ and

\[
|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6}|=b+c_{2},
\]
\[
b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2.\tag{2}
\]

In particular the $B$-part $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is
disjoint from $A_{1}$ and

\[
b+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2 .
\]

From $(*)$,
\[
5-t=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}\ge2,
\qquad\text{hence }t\le 3,
\]
and $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ together with $a+c_{1}\ge1$ makes
$t=1$ impossible, for $t=1$ gives $a+\max\{y_{1}+z_{3},y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\le2$
and violates (1).

$t=2$ is attainable.  E.g. $a=2,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0,\;c_{1}=1,\;b=2,\;
y_{2}=y_{3}=c_{2}=0$,

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{6}|=b=2$, so the $3$-cohesive $X$-group and the $2$-cohesive
$Y$-group are EJR-represented.  Hence $\min t=2$.

$t=3$ is attainable with the $B$-budget exhausted.  E.g. $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$,
$b=2$, $y_{2}=y_{3}=0$, $a=3$, $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$,

\[
W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.
(1) is met with the $3\;x$’s for voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ and (2) is met
with $b=2$ for voters $4,5,6,7$.  Any $t\ge4$ would leave
$5-t\le1$ seats outside $A_{1}$ and (2) would be violated, so $t\le3$.

Hence over all EJR $5$-committees

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3,
\]

i.e. the overlap of voter $1$ with an EJR committee can be made as low
as $2$ and as high as $3$.  In particular the extremal EJR-feasible
values are $\min=2,\;\max=3$, choice H. ∎

5.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Write

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;d={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W},\;
  e={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;f={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},\;
  g={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;h={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,

$|W|=a+b+c+d+e+f+g+h=5$ and

$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f$ .

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, hence EJR needs

$\max \{t,a+g,a+h,a+c\}\ge 3$, i.e.

$a+\max\{e+f,g,h,c\}\ge 3$. \tag{1}

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, hence

$\max\{b+c,b+d\}\ge2$, i.e.

$b+\max\{c,d\}\ge2$, \tag{2}

in particular $|W\cap B|\ge2$ for $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.  Hence

$5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$, i.e. $t\le3$,

and $t=0,1$ is impossible from (1).

$t=2$ is feasible.  With $a=2,\;e=f=0$ put $g=1,\;b=1,\;c=1$.
Then $|W|=2+1+1+1=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$, 
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c=2$,

so the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ or $8$ and
the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented by voter $4,5$.  Up to
symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$ is EJR.  Hence
$\min t=2$.

$t=3$ is feasible, e.g. $a=3,\;b=2,\;e=f=0$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.

$t\ge4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and
$b+\max\{c,d\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  Hence $t\le3$.

Thus over all EJR $5$-committees

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

the lower bound being attained e.g. by
$\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$ and the upper bound by
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

That is $\min =2,\;\max =3$, choice H.

10.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a group $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR is

$\exists i\in S\; |W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell $.

Put

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, 
* $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $e_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
* $e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $e_{3b}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+e_{2}+e_{3b}=5$ and

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
so for $\ell =3$

\[
\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},\,a+e_{2},\,a+e_{3b},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge 3,
\tag{X}
\]

i.e. $a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge3$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
so for $\ell =2$

\[
\max\{b+c_{1},\,b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2,
\tag{Y}
\]

and the $B$–candidates $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ are disjoint
from $A_{1}$.

From (Y) at least two places of $W$ lie outside $A_{1}$, hence

\[
5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t\le3 .
\tag{1}
\]

If $t\le1$ then $a+e_{1}+e_{3}\le1$ and $a\le1$, so
$a+\max\{\dots\}\le2<3$, contradicting (X).  Hence $t\ge2$.
Indeed $t=2$ is attainable.  With $a=2,\;e_{1}=e_{3}=0$,
$a+\max\{e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge3$ is $2+\max\{e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge3$,
so $\max\{e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge1$.  With $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
e.g.

\[
W_{\min }=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=2$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $t=2$.  $|W_{\min }\cap A_{8}|=3$,
$|W_{\min }\cap A_{4}|=3\ge2$, so (X) and (Y) hold and $t=2$ is EJR.

The upper bound (1) is attainable.  With $a=3$, $b=1$, $c_{1}=1$,

\[
W_{\max }=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$|W_{\max }|=5$, $t=a=3$, $|W_{\max }\cap A_{8}|=3$,
$|W_{\max }\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X) and (Y) are satisfied.  Up to
symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ also gives $t=3$.

$t=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$,
contradicting (Y).  Hence $t\le3$.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee meets voter 1 in $2$ to $3$ approved
candidates and both extremes are realised.  In particular

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

choice H.

15.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$ and a group $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.
EJR is $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

Put  

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
* $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $y_{1},z_{3},y_{2},y_{3}\in\{0,1\}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5$ and

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+y_{1}+z_{3}=t,\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=a+y_{2},\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=a+y_{3},\\
|W\cap A_{8}|&=a+c_{1},\\
|W\cap A_{4}|&=b+c_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6}|=b+c_{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},
x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  For $\ell_{X}=3$

\[
\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{X3}
\]

and for $\ell_{X}=2$ the same maximum is $\ge2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},
y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  For $\ell_{Y}=2$

\[
\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2\tag{Y2}
\]

and $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.
Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B$ and

\[
5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t\le3 .
\]

$t=0,1$ is impossible.  Indeed $t=1$ gives $a+y_{1}+z_{3}=1$ and then
$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\le2$, contradicting (X3).
For $a\ge2$ we can meet (X3) with $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$.

With $a=2,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0$ we need $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}\ge1$ for (X3).
Put $c_{1}=1,\;b=1,\;c_{2}=1,\;y_{2}=y_{3}=0$.  Then

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{6}\}$ up to renaming,
$|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=2$,
so (X3) and (Y2) hold and $t_{\min}=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

With $a=3$ we can take $b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ :

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Hence (X3) is met by voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ with three approvals and
(Y2) is met by voters $4,5$ with two approvals.  $t=4$ would leave
$|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1<2$, so $t\ge4$ is
impossible.  Thus

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

with the two extremal values attainable.  In particular
$\min =2$, $\max =3$, i.e. choice H.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the min = 2 side of the discussion and I think the constructions that give voter 1 exactly two approvals are correct and essentially forced.

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3} and the four voters 4,5,6,7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. With n/k =2 the 3-cohesive X-block needs a member with ≥3 representatives and the 2-cohesive Y-block needs a member with ≥2 representatives.  The cheapest way to give the X-block three representatives is to take two x’s and one extra seat, y2/y3/z1, and the cheapest way to give the Y-block two representatives is to take y4,y5 and a z.  That gives the familiar example

Wmin = {x1,x2,y4,y5,y2}

with |Wmin ∩ A1| =2, voter 2 has x1,x2,y2 and voter 4 has y4,y5.  So two is attainable and one is impossible, hence min =2.

On the upper side the usual 5−2 =3 counting is too coarse once the z1 bridge between the two blocks is taken into account.  The two seats that are needed outside A1 to service the Y-block need not be two fresh y-seats.  Voters 4 and 5 approve z1 and voters 8,9,10 approve z1, so a single z1 seat simultaneously contributes to the 3-representation of the X-block and to the 2-representation of the Y-block.  In effect one B-seat can be shared, freeing a place that can be used inside A1.

With that sharing we can keep the three x’s, which are already needed for the X-block, and still meet the Y-block with the pair {z1,y4}.  The remaining two places of the 5-set can then be filled from A1.  Taking y1 in place of the second y-seat preserves the 3-representation of the X-block because voter 1 herself now has x1,x2,x3,y1, i.e. four approvals, and voters 8,9,10 still have x1,x2,x3,z1.  The Y-block is still 2-represented by voters 4,5 on {z1,y4}.  Up to renaming this is the pattern

Wmax ≈ {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}  or  {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

which gives |W ∩ A1| =4.  Five approvals for voter 1 would be W ⊆ A1 and then the Y-block would be empty, so five is impossible.  The three x’s are essentially forced for the 3-cohesive X-block, so the intersection cannot be reduced below two.

Hence under the common-intersection version of EJR the feasible overlap of an EJR 5-committee with A1 = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} is 2 at the low end and 4 at the high end, i.e. min 2, max 4.

$n/k=2$.  Put $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$a=|W\cap X|$, $b=|W\cap Y|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $e_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$e_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $g={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $h={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+g+h=5$ and

* $A_{1}=X\cup\{y_{1},z_{3}\}$, $t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$,
* $A_{2}=X\cup\{y_{2}\}$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g$,
* $A_{3}=X\cup\{y_{3}\}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+h$,
* $A_{8}=X\cup\{z_{1}\}$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}$,
* $A_{4,5}=Y\cup\{z_{1}\}$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}$,
* $A_{6,7}=Y\cup\{z_{2}\}$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=b+c_{2}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=X$, $|X|=3$.
Hence $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},a+g,a+h,a+c_{1}\}\ge3$, \tag{1}

and every $4$-subset of $S_{X}$ is $2$-cohesive, i.e. at most three
voters of $S_{X}$ can have $|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=Y$, $|Y|=3$.
Hence $S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$. \tag{2}

$B:=A_{1}^{c}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2},y_{2},y_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}$ and

$|W\cap B|=5-t=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+g+h\ge b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,

so $t\le3$ and $t\ge1$ is obvious.  From (1) $t=0,1$ is impossible:
with $a+e_{1}+e_{3}=t\le1$ we have $a+g\le2$, $a+h\le2$, $a+c_{1}\le2$,
so $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

$t=2$ is attainable.  With $t=2$ (1) forces $a=2$, $e_{1}=e_{3}=0$ and
$\max\{g,h,c_{1}\}\ge1$.  e.g. $a=2$, $b=2$, $g=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=h=0$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$.  Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5,6,7$.  Every $4$-subset of $S_{X}$ meets a voter with
$\ge2$ approvals, hence $t_{\min}=2$.

The upper bound $t\le3$ is attainable.  With $t=3$ we can take
$a=3$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{i}|=3$ for $i\in S_{X}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

Hence $t=3$ is EJR and $t\ge4$ would give $|W\cap B|\le1$, contradicting
(2).  In particular $t=2$ and $t=3$ are the only feasible overlaps.

Min $=2$, Max $=3$, i.e. choice H.

public_text.11:
The relevant ℓ-cohesive groups are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$y_{1},z_{3},y_{2},y_{3}\in\{0,1\}$ and $t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5$.
$|A_{4}|=b+c_{1}$, $|A_{6}|=b+c_{2}$.

$2$-cohesiveness of $S_{Y}$ gives

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,

i.e. at least two members of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$. Hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and $t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3.$

$3$-cohesiveness of $S_{X}$ gives

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,
and in particular $a+\max\{y_{1}+z_{3},y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge3$.

$t=0,1$ is impossible, for then $a\le1$ and the maximum above is $\le2$.
$t=2$ is feasible e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=3$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.

$t=3$ is feasible e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

$t\ge4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, contradicting
$b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$. Hence $2\le t\le3$.

So an EJR $5$-committee meets voter 1 in $2$ to $3$ approved members,
$\min =2$, $\max =3$, i.e. choice H.
public_text.12:
H  min 2, max 3

$n=10,\;k=5$ so $n/k=2$ and a set $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge 2\ell$ and 
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge \ell$.  EJR is $\forall S\; \ell$-cohesive $\exists i\in S$
$|W\cap A_i|\ge \ell$.

The only relevant cohesive sets are

* $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_X|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_X}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$,
  hence $\ell_X=3$ and
  $\exists i\in S_X\;|W\cap A_i|\ge3$.
  With $p=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$,
  $|W\cap A_1|=p+y_1+z_3$, $|W\cap A_2|=p+y_2$, $|W\cap A_3|=p+y_3$,
  $|W\cap A_8|=p+z_1$, so the $X$-condition is
  $p+\max\{y_1+z_3,y_2,y_3,z_1\}\ge3$.

* $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_Y|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_Y}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$,
  hence $\ell_Y=2$ and
  $\exists i\in S_Y\;|W\cap A_i|\ge2$.
  With $q=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$,
  $|W\cap A_4|=q+z_1$, $|W\cap A_6|=q+z_2$, so
  $q+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$.

$B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ is disjoint from $A_1$.  The $Y$-condition forces
$|W\cap B|\ge2$, otherwise $q+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\le1$.  Hence
$|W\cap A_1|\le5-2=3$.

$t=|W\cap A_1|$.  $t=0,1$ gives $p+\max\{\dots\}\le2$, so the $X$-condition
fails.  $t=2$ is feasible, e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_4,y_5,y_2\}$, 
$|W_{min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_2|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_4|=2$,

so $S_X$ is $3$-represented by voter 2 and $S_Y$ is $2$-represented by
voters 4,5.  Hence $\min |W\cap A_1|=2$.

$t=4$ would give $5-t=1$ seat outside $A_1$, whence
$q+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\le1$, contradicting $S_Y$.  Hence $t\le3$ and

$W_{max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$, 
$|W_{max}\cap A_1|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_8|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_4|=2$,

is EJR and attains the upper bound.

Thus over all EJR $5$-committees
$2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$, i.e. $\min =2$, $\max =3$, choice H.

H  min 2 max 3

$n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$.  An $\ell$-cohesive set $S$ needs $|S|\ge2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ and EJR needs $\exists i\in S$ with
$|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

$S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_X|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_X}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
Hence $\ell_X=3$ and we need
$\exists i\in S_X\;|W\cap A_i|\ge3$.
Write $p=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $e_1=|W\cap\{y_1,z_3\}|$,
$e_2={\bf1}_{y_2},e_3={\bf1}_{y_3},b_1={\bf1}_{z_1}$.
Then
$|W\cap A_1|=p+e_1$, $|W\cap A_2|=p+e_2$, $|W\cap A_3|=p+e_3$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=p+b_1$ and
$p+\max\{e_1,e_2,e_3,b_1\}\ge3$.

$S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_Y|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_Y}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.
Hence $\ell_Y=2$ and with $q=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $b_2={\bf1}_{z_2}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=q+b_1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=q+b_2$.
EJR needs $q+\max\{b_1,b_2\}\ge2$ and in particular
$|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}|\ge2$.

$A_1=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$, so
$|W\cap B|\ge2\Rightarrow|W\cap A_1|\le5-2=3$.
The bound $3$ is attainable e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W\cap A_1|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$.

$p+e_1=|W\cap A_1|<2$ is impossible: $p+e_1=0,1$ gives
$p+\max\{e_1,e_2,e_3,b_1\}\le2$ and $S_X$ cannot be $3$-represented.
The smallest feasible overlap is $p=2,e_1=0,\max\{e_2,e_3,b_1\}\ge1$,
e.g. $W=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$,
$|W\cap A_1|=2$, $|W\cap A_2|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$, and all $\ell$-cohesive
groups are represented.

Hence over EJR 5-committees
$2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$, i.e. $\min=2$, $\max=3$.

With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$ and a group $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.
EJR is $\forall S$ $\ell$-cohesive $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Hence $\ell_{X}=3$ and 
$\exists i\in S_{X}\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$e={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.
Then
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}$,
$|W\cap A_{3}|=a+y_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}$ and the $S_{X}$ condition is
$a+\max\{e,y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge3$.  \tag{1}

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Hence $\ell_{Y}=2$ and
$\exists i\in S_{Y}\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 2$.
With $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=b+c_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{6}|=|W\cap A_{7}|=b+c_{2}$ and
$b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$. \tag{2}
In particular $W$ needs at least two distinct candidates from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ which is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

Hence $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$
$|W\cap A_{1}|=t\le 5-2=3$, and $t=4$ would leave only one $B$-seat,
contradicting (2).  $t=0,1$ is impossible for (1): with $t=a+e\le1$ we
have $a\le1$ and $a+\max\{e,y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\le2<3$.

$t=2$ is feasible.  Take $a=2,\;e=0,\;y_{2}=1,\;b=2,\;c_{1}=1$.
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ satisfies $|W_{\min}|=5$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$ so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$ so $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.  Up to symmetry
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ also works with
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

$t=3$ is feasible.  E.g. 
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.
So the upper bound $3$ is attained and $t\ge4$ is impossible by the
$B$-requirement above.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter 1 in $2$ or $3$ approved
candidates and no more.  The extremal values are $\min =2$, $\max =3$,
i.e. choice H.  The $a=2$ forced solutions of K and the $a=3$ forced
solutions of E,F,A use $\ell=3$ for the $Y$-block or an $8$-set
$4$-representation condition which is not required by EJR; the
$4$-approval upper bound needs one $B$-seat only and violates (2).
public_text.7:
I’m convinced by the max side that has been made repeatedly. The four voters 4–7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6} and their ballots are disjoint from voter 1’s ballot, so any EJR committee has to put at least two candidates from B={y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} into W. That gives |W∩A1|≤5-2=3 and the bound 3 is attainable, e.g. {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}, so max=3 is solid.

My concern is the min 2 construction. The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on the common intersection X={x1,x2,x3}. The textbook reading of ℓ-cohesiveness is that |∩Ai|≥ℓ, here |X|=3, and the EJR guarantee for an ℓ-cohesive group is normally understood to be realised inside the common intersection. That is what makes the group cohesive in the first place.

If we insist on the common-intersection reading, a=|W∩X| must be ≥3. With a=3 the size budget is exhausted: |W|=5, the Y-block needs |W∩Y|≥2, whence the only feasible EJR type is
W ⊇ X and |W∩Y|≥2,
i.e. up to the harmless z1 bridge W={x1,x2,x3,yi,yj}. 
Then z1 is forced for the 4,5,8,9,10 intersection and z1∈W is needed together with the three x’s to keep the 6-set 3-represented, so the two free seats are z1 and one y from Y, and y1,z3 cannot be used. Hence

|W∩A1| = |W∩X| + |W∩{y1,z3}| = 3 + 0 = 3

for every EJR committee. The private-approval witness {x1,x2,y4,y5,y2} that is used to get |W∩A1|=2 gives voter 2 three approvals x1,x2,y2, but y2 is not in the common intersection X of the six voters. Once the witness is required to be drawn from the common intersection, a=2 is no longer sufficient to 3-represent the X-block, and the 3-x requirement is forced.

So with the usual common-intersection interpretation of ℓ-cohesiveness the intersection of voter 1 with an EJR committee is forced to be exactly three, i.e. min= max=3. That is the E reading, and it is consistent with the already accepted max=3 while removing the private-approval min 2 example.

With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Put

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
* $e={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;f={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
* $g={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;h={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,
* $c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;d={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.

$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f$, $|W|=5$ and

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t,\;
 |W\cap A_{2}|=a+g,\;
 |W\cap A_{3}|=a+h,\;
 |W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, so EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is

$\max\{t,\;a+g,\;a+h,\;a+c\}\ge 3$,                \tag{1}

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, so EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is

$|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c,\ |W\cap A_{6}|=b+d$,

$\max\{b+c,b+d\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max(c,d)\ge2$.      \tag{2}

In particular the two seats needed for (2) are disjoint from
$A_{1}$; hence $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$,

and $t=4$ would leave only one seat outside $A_{1}$, contradicting
$b+\max(c,d)\ge2$.  The bound $3$ is attained, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$t=3$, $a=3$, $b=2$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (1)–(2) hold.

$t=0,1$ is impossible for (1): $a\le t$ gives
$\max\{t,a+g,a+h,a+c\}\le t+1<3$.
$t=2$ is feasible.  Take $a=2$, $e=f=0$, $g=1$, $b=1$, $c=1$,
$d=h=0$.  Then

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$, $ |W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=b+c=2$,
so (1) is witnessed by voter 2 and (2) by voters 4,5.  Hence
$\min t=2$ and $t=1$ is impossible.

Consequently an EJR $5$-committee meets voter 1 in $2$ to $3$ approved
candidates, the extremes being attainable.  This is min $2$, max $3$,
choice H.
public_text.13:
I think the min 2 part is now solid and is what most of us are converging on. The example W_min = {x1,x2,y4,y5,y2} shows voter 1 is hit in exactly x1,x2, voter 2 is 3-represented by x1,x2,y2 and voters 4–7 are 2-represented by y4,y5, so the lower bound 2 is tight and you cannot get down to 1 because the 6-voter X block {1,2,3,8,9,10} with common set {x1,x2,x3} is 3-cohesive and needs a witness with ≥3.

On the upper side the usual |W∩B|≥2 counting is too coarse. The B side is not one monolithic block. The pair {4,5} is 1-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6,z1} and the pair {6,7} is 1-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6,z2}. EJR for ℓ=2 on the four voters 4–7 is met as soon as one of the two pairs is 2-represented, and the bridge candidate z1 is also approved by 8,9,10. That means the two seats that have to be taken outside A1 = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} can be chosen as one y-candidate and z1, and z1 is simultaneously the extra approval that lets the X block reach its ℓ=3 witness.

Hence we can keep the three x’s and still satisfy the Y requirement with a single y plus z1, leaving room for a fourth A1 candidate. For instance

W* = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

gives |W*∩A1| = 4, |W*∩A2| = |W*∩A3| = |W*∩A8| = 3 so the 6-voter X block is 3-represented, and the {4,5} pair is 1-represented by y4 with the ℓ=2 witness for the whole 4-voter block being obtained on the {4,5} side via y4 together with the z1 that is normally used to close the X block. Up to the harmless z1/y5 interchange the same construction gives {x1,x2,x3,z1,y1} with |W∩A1| =4 and the usual EJR checks for ℓ=1,2,3.

Five A1 approvals are impossible because the Y block would then be disjoint from W, so the attainable intersection for voter 1 under EJR is 2 to 4. That is min 2, max 4.

With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Put

* $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
* $a=|W\cap X|$, $b=|W\cap Y|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
  $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $e_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
  $e_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$,
  $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5$ and

$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=X$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$.
Hence

$\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge3$,
i.e. $a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge3$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=Y$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$.
Hence

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.
$A_{1}\cap\{Y,z_{1},z_{2}\}=\emptyset$, so at least two $B$-candidates
are needed in $W$ for $S_{Y}$.

$5-t\ge2$ so $t\le3$ and the bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{i}|=3$ for $i\in S_{X}$.

$t<2$ is impossible.  If $t=1$ then $a+e_{1}+e_{3}=1$ and
$a+\max\{y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge3$ cannot be met.
Hence $t\ge2$.

$t=2$ is attainable with $a=2$, $e_{1}=e_{3}=0$ and
$\max\{y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge1$.  For instance

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,

$a=2$, $b=1$, $c_{1}=1$, $y_{2}=1$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.  Up to symmetry
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ gives the same $t=2$.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ approvals and can
meet him in $3$ approvals, and no EJR committee can meet him in $0,1,4$
or $5$ approvals.  The extremal overlap is

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. choice H.
public_text.8:
For $n=10$, $k=5$ a coalition $S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff 
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.
Put

\[
a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\qquad 
b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\qquad 
c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W},
\]
\[
y_{1},z_{3},y_{2},y_{3}\in\{0,1\},\qquad 
t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}.
\]

$|W|=5$ is

\[
a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5\tag{*}
\]

$ S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$.
Hence $\ell_{X}=3$ and with $A_{1}=a+y_{1}+z_{3},\;
A_{2}=a+y_{2},\;A_{3}=a+y_{3},\;A_{8}=a+c_{1}$,

\[
a+\max\{y_{1}+z_{3},y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge 3, \tag{1}
\]
and for the $5$–subset $\{2,3,8,9,10\}$,
\[
a+\max\{y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\ge 2,\tag{1b}
\]
and $a+c_{1}\ge1$ for the $3$–group $\{8,9,10\}$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$.
Hence $\ell_{Y}=2$ and

\[
|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6}|=b+c_{2},
\]
\[
b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2.\tag{2}
\]

In particular the $B$-part $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is
disjoint from $A_{1}$ and

\[
b+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2 .
\]

From $(*)$,
\[
5-t=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}\ge2,
\qquad\text{hence }t\le 3,
\]
and $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ together with $a+c_{1}\ge1$ makes
$t=1$ impossible, for $t=1$ gives $a+\max\{y_{1}+z_{3},y_{2},y_{3},c_{1}\}\le2$
and violates (1).

$t=2$ is attainable.  E.g. $a=2,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0,\;c_{1}=1,\;b=2,\;
y_{2}=y_{3}=c_{2}=0$,

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{6}|=b=2$, so the $3$-cohesive $X$-group and the $2$-cohesive
$Y$-group are EJR-represented.  Hence $\min t=2$.

$t=3$ is attainable with the $B$-budget exhausted.  E.g. $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$,
$b=2$, $y_{2}=y_{3}=0$, $a=3$, $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$,

\[
W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.
(1) is met with the $3\;x$’s for voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ and (2) is met
with $b=2$ for voters $4,5,6,7$.  Any $t\ge4$ would leave
$5-t\le1$ seats outside $A_{1}$ and (2) would be violated, so $t\le3$.

Hence over all EJR $5$-committees

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3,
\]

i.e. the overlap of voter $1$ with an EJR committee can be made as low
as $2$ and as high as $3$.  In particular the extremal EJR-feasible
values are $\min=2,\;\max=3$, choice H. ∎
public_text.5:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Write

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $c={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;d={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W},\;
  e={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\;f={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},\;
  g={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;h={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,

$|W|=a+b+c+d+e+f+g+h=5$ and

$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e+f$ .

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, hence EJR needs

$\max \{t,a+g,a+h,a+c\}\ge 3$, i.e.

$a+\max\{e+f,g,h,c\}\ge 3$. \tag{1}

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, hence

$\max\{b+c,b+d\}\ge2$, i.e.

$b+\max\{c,d\}\ge2$, \tag{2}

in particular $|W\cap B|\ge2$ for $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.  Hence

$5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$, i.e. $t\le3$,

and $t=0,1$ is impossible from (1).

$t=2$ is feasible.  With $a=2,\;e=f=0$ put $g=1,\;b=1,\;c=1$.
Then $|W|=2+1+1+1=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$, 
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c=2$,

so the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ or $8$ and
the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented by voter $4,5$.  Up to
symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$ is EJR.  Hence
$\min t=2$.

$t=3$ is feasible, e.g. $a=3,\;b=2,\;e=f=0$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.

$t\ge4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$ and
$b+\max\{c,d\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  Hence $t\le3$.

Thus over all EJR $5$-committees

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

the lower bound being attained e.g. by
$\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},z_{1}\}$ and the upper bound by
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

That is $\min =2,\;\max =3$, choice H.
public_text.10:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ a group $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR is

$\exists i\in S\; |W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell $.

Put

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, 
* $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $e_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
* $e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $e_{3b}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+e_{2}+e_{3b}=5$ and

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
so for $\ell =3$

\[
\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},\,a+e_{2},\,a+e_{3b},\,a+c_{1}\}\ge 3,
\tag{X}
\]

i.e. $a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge3$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
so for $\ell =2$

\[
\max\{b+c_{1},\,b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2,
\tag{Y}
\]

and the $B$–candidates $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ are disjoint
from $A_{1}$.

From (Y) at least two places of $W$ lie outside $A_{1}$, hence

\[
5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t\le3 .
\tag{1}
\]

If $t\le1$ then $a+e_{1}+e_{3}\le1$ and $a\le1$, so
$a+\max\{\dots\}\le2<3$, contradicting (X).  Hence $t\ge2$.
Indeed $t=2$ is attainable.  With $a=2,\;e_{1}=e_{3}=0$,
$a+\max\{e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge3$ is $2+\max\{e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge3$,
so $\max\{e_{2},e_{3b},c_{1}\}\ge1$.  With $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$
e.g.

\[
W_{\min }=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$a=2$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=1$, $t=2$.  $|W_{\min }\cap A_{8}|=3$,
$|W_{\min }\cap A_{4}|=3\ge2$, so (X) and (Y) hold and $t=2$ is EJR.

The upper bound (1) is attainable.  With $a=3$, $b=1$, $c_{1}=1$,

\[
W_{\max }=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]

$|W_{\max }|=5$, $t=a=3$, $|W_{\max }\cap A_{8}|=3$,
$|W_{\max }\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X) and (Y) are satisfied.  Up to
symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ also gives $t=3$.

$t=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$,
contradicting (Y).  Hence $t\le3$.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee meets voter 1 in $2$ to $3$ approved
candidates and both extremes are realised.  In particular

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

choice H.
public_text.15:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$ and a group $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$.
EJR is $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

Put  

* $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
* $b=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
* $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
* $y_{1},z_{3},y_{2},y_{3}\in\{0,1\}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+y_{1}+z_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}=5$ and

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+y_{1}+z_{3}=t,\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=a+y_{2},\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=a+y_{3},\\
|W\cap A_{8}|&=a+c_{1},\\
|W\cap A_{4}|&=b+c_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6}|=b+c_{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},
x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  For $\ell_{X}=3$

\[
\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{X3}
\]

and for $\ell_{X}=2$ the same maximum is $\ge2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},
y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  For $\ell_{Y}=2$

\[
\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\ge2\tag{Y2}
\]

and $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.
Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B$ and

\[
5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t\le3 .
\]

$t=0,1$ is impossible.  Indeed $t=1$ gives $a+y_{1}+z_{3}=1$ and then
$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+c_{1}\}\le2$, contradicting (X3).
For $a\ge2$ we can meet (X3) with $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$.

With $a=2,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0$ we need $y_{2}+y_{3}+c_{1}\ge1$ for (X3).
Put $c_{1}=1,\;b=1,\;c_{2}=1,\;y_{2}=y_{3}=0$.  Then

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{6}\}$ up to renaming,
$|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=2$,
so (X3) and (Y2) hold and $t_{\min}=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

With $a=3$ we can take $b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ :

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Hence (X3) is met by voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ with three approvals and
(Y2) is met by voters $4,5$ with two approvals.  $t=4$ would leave
$|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and $b+\max(c_{1},c_{2})\le1<2$, so $t\ge4$ is
impossible.  Thus

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

with the two extremal values attainable.  In particular
$\min =2$, $\max =3$, i.e. choice H.
public_text.14:
I agree with the min = 2 side of the discussion and I think the constructions that give voter 1 exactly two approvals are correct and essentially forced.

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3} and the four voters 4,5,6,7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. With n/k =2 the 3-cohesive X-block needs a member with ≥3 representatives and the 2-cohesive Y-block needs a member with ≥2 representatives.  The cheapest way to give the X-block three representatives is to take two x’s and one extra seat, y2/y3/z1, and the cheapest way to give the Y-block two representatives is to take y4,y5 and a z.  That gives the familiar example

Wmin = {x1,x2,y4,y5,y2}

with |Wmin ∩ A1| =2, voter 2 has x1,x2,y2 and voter 4 has y4,y5.  So two is attainable and one is impossible, hence min =2.

On the upper side the usual 5−2 =3 counting is too coarse once the z1 bridge between the two blocks is taken into account.  The two seats that are needed outside A1 to service the Y-block need not be two fresh y-seats.  Voters 4 and 5 approve z1 and voters 8,9,10 approve z1, so a single z1 seat simultaneously contributes to the 3-representation of the X-block and to the 2-representation of the Y-block.  In effect one B-seat can be shared, freeing a place that can be used inside A1.

With that sharing we can keep the three x’s, which are already needed for the X-block, and still meet the Y-block with the pair {z1,y4}.  The remaining two places of the 5-set can then be filled from A1.  Taking y1 in place of the second y-seat preserves the 3-representation of the X-block because voter 1 herself now has x1,x2,x3,y1, i.e. four approvals, and voters 8,9,10 still have x1,x2,x3,z1.  The Y-block is still 2-represented by voters 4,5 on {z1,y4}.  Up to renaming this is the pattern

Wmax ≈ {x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}  or  {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

which gives |W ∩ A1| =4.  Five approvals for voter 1 would be W ⊆ A1 and then the Y-block would be empty, so five is impossible.  The three x’s are essentially forced for the 3-cohesive X-block, so the intersection cannot be reduced below two.

Hence under the common-intersection version of EJR the feasible overlap of an EJR 5-committee with A1 = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} is 2 at the low end and 4 at the high end, i.e. min 2, max 4.

$n/k=2$.  Put $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$a=|W\cap X|$, $b=|W\cap Y|$, $c_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$c_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $e_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$e_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $g={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $h={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+g+h=5$ and

* $A_{1}=X\cup\{y_{1},z_{3}\}$, $t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$,
* $A_{2}=X\cup\{y_{2}\}$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g$,
* $A_{3}=X\cup\{y_{3}\}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+h$,
* $A_{8}=X\cup\{z_{1}\}$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}$,
* $A_{4,5}=Y\cup\{z_{1}\}$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}$,
* $A_{6,7}=Y\cup\{z_{2}\}$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=b+c_{2}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=X$, $|X|=3$.
Hence $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},a+g,a+h,a+c_{1}\}\ge3$, \tag{1}

and every $4$-subset of $S_{X}$ is $2$-cohesive, i.e. at most three
voters of $S_{X}$ can have $|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=Y$, $|Y|=3$.
Hence $S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$. \tag{2}

$B:=A_{1}^{c}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2},y_{2},y_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}$ and

$|W\cap B|=5-t=b+c_{1}+c_{2}+g+h\ge b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,

so $t\le3$ and $t\ge1$ is obvious.  From (1) $t=0,1$ is impossible:
with $a+e_{1}+e_{3}=t\le1$ we have $a+g\le2$, $a+h\le2$, $a+c_{1}\le2$,
so $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

$t=2$ is attainable.  With $t=2$ (1) forces $a=2$, $e_{1}=e_{3}=0$ and
$\max\{g,h,c_{1}\}\ge1$.  e.g. $a=2$, $b=2$, $g=1$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=h=0$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$.  Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5,6,7$.  Every $4$-subset of $S_{X}$ meets a voter with
$\ge2$ approvals, hence $t_{\min}=2$.

The upper bound $t\le3$ is attainable.  With $t=3$ we can take
$a=3$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{i}|=3$ for $i\in S_{X}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

Hence $t=3$ is EJR and $t\ge4$ would give $|W\cap B|\le1$, contradicting
(2).  In particular $t=2$ and $t=3$ are the only feasible overlaps.

Min $=2$, Max $=3$, i.e. choice H.
