Then
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+1_{y_{1}\in W}+1_{z_{3}\in W}=3$
for every EJR committee, because $y_{1},z_{3}\notin B$ cannot be used to
meet the $2$-requirement of $S_{Y}$.

With the max $=3$ already agreed, that makes the overlap with voter 1
constant:
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

That is the common-intersection reading of EJR for the $3$-cohesive $X$-block,
and it is consistent with the $B$-disjointness proof for the upper bound.
The $t=2$ private-approval witnesses are the $\exists i\in S$ relaxation
that moves the third approval of $S_{X}$ off the common core $X$ onto a
private $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ approval. Under the usual
cohesiveness-intersection definition those witnesses do not give $S_{X}$
a genuine $3$-representation on $X$.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the Y-block counting that has become consensus. 
With $n/k=2$, $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive on $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and
$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2$ so $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$.
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
hence $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and $5-t\ge2$, i.e. $t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ shows $t=3$ is attainable, so max $=3$ is settled.

The minimum is then decided by how the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is read.
$|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$ and $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}=X$, $|\!X\!|=3$.
In the approval definition a set is $\ell$-cohesive precisely because it has
$\ell$ candidates in common, here the three $x$’s.  The EJR guarantee for an
$\ell$-cohesive coalition is meant to be realised on that common core; otherwise
the $\ell$ seats would not be shared by the whole coalition.

Hence for $S_{X}$ we need $a=|W\cap X|\ge3$.  With $a\ge3$ the budget
$|W|=5$ together with $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ forces, up to symmetry,
$a=3$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$, i.e. essentially
$W\supset X$ and $|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|\ge2$.

The private-approval witnesses often quoted,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ with $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$,
or $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$,
give one member of $S_{X}$ three approved seats, but the extra seat is
$y_{2}$ resp. $z_{1}$, which is not in $\bigcap S_{X}=X$.  Voters 1,3,8,9,10
do not share $y_{2}$ or $z_{1}$ with the whole coalition, so the three seats
are not a common $3$-representation of $S_{X}$.

Once $a\ge3$ is enforced, $y_{1}$ and $z_{3}$ can never appear in an EJR
committee without breaking the $2$-representation of $S_{Y}$, because
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ and $|W\cap B|\ge2$.  Then

$|W\cap A_{1}| = a + 1_{y_{1}\in W}+1_{z_{3}\in W}=3+0=3$

for every EJR $5$-committee.  With the agreed upper bound $t\le3$ this gives
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. the common-core reading of EJR
forces the overlap of voter 1 to be exactly three.

9.text:
With $n=10,k=5$ put $n/k=2$

$a=|W\cap X|$, $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$b=|W\cap Y|$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W},c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$e_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W},e_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$g=1_{y_{2}\in W},h=1_{y_{3}\in W}$,

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+g+h=5$,
$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$.

$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+h$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+c_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+c_{2}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap S_{X}=X$, $\ell_{X}=3$
\[
\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},a+g,a+h,a+c_{1}\}\ge3\iff
a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},g,h,c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{X}
\]

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=Y$, $\ell_{Y}=2$
\[
\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}
\]

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  (Y) gives $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and
hence

$5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap B|\ge2\;\Longrightarrow\;t\le3$,

$t\ge4$ would give $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$ contradicting (Y).

$t\le1$ is impossible for (X): $t\le1\Rightarrow a\le1$ and
$a+\max\{\cdot\}\le2<3$, so $t\ge2$.

The bounds are attainable under the usual $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
formulation.

$t=2$: $a=2,b=2,g=1$, e.g.
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=b=2$.
Up to symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=3$, $t=2$.

$t=3$: $a=3,b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$, e.g.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=a=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=b=2$.  (X) and (Y) hold and the bound is tight.

Hence with the standard approval EJR witness
\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]
both extremes are realisable.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. choice H.

The $t=4$ examples e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ give
$b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$ and therefore violate the 2-representation of
the 2-cohesive $S_{Y}$.  The $a\ge3$ common-core forcing that gives
$\min=\max=3$, choice E, is the stricter requirement that the three
representatives of $S_{X}$ be taken from $\bigcap S_{X}=X$, which is not
part of the usual $\exists i$ EJR witness condition.

6.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ put

$a=|W\cap X|$, $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$b=|W\cap Y|$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$c_{1}=1_{z_{1}\in W}$, $c_{2}=1_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$e_{1}=1_{y_{1}\in W}$, $e_{3}=1_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$g=1_{y_{2}\in W}$, $h=1_{y_{3}\in W}$,

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+g+h=5$,
$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$.

$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+h$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+c_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+c_{2}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap S_{X}=X$, $\ell_{X}=3$,

\[
\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},a+g,a+h,a+c_{1}\}\ge3
\iff a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},g,h,c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{X}
\]

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap S_{Y}=Y$, $\ell_{Y}=2$,

\[
\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2.\tag{Y}
\]

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
(Y) gives $|W\cap B|=b+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ and

$5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap B|\ge2$, i.e. $t\le3$,

and $t=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and
$b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  Hence $\max t=3$ and
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ is tight with
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

$t\le1$ is impossible for (X): $t\le1\Rightarrow a\le1$ and
$a+\max\{\cdot\}\le2<3$, so $t\ge2$.

$t=2$ is attainable with the usual $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
witness.  E.g. $a=2$, $b=2$, $g=1$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=b=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.  Up to symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$
gives $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=3$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

Hence under the standard approval EJR definition

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

both extremes are realised.  In particular

$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

choice H.  The $a\ge3$ common-core reading that would force
$\min=\max=3$, choice E, is the stricter requirement that the
$\ell$ witnesses be taken from $\bigcap S_{X}$; with the standard
$\exists i$ witness the private approvals $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}$ are
admissible and the $2$-overlap is attainable.  The upper bound $3$
and the $B$-disjointness argument are now settled.

1.text:
With $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$,

$a=|W\cap X|$, $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$b=|W\cap Y|$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$c_{1}= {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},c_{2}= {\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$e_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},e_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W},g= {\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},
h= {\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,

$|W|=a+b+c_{1}+c_{2}+e_{1}+e_{3}+g+h=5$,
$t:=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap S_{X}=X$, $\ell_{X}=3$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+e_{1}+e_{3},\;|W\cap A_{2}|=a+g,\;
|W\cap A_{3}|=a+h,\;|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+c_{1}$,

EJR on $S_{X}$ is

$\max\{a+e_{1}+e_{3},a+g,a+h,a+c_{1}\}\ge 3
\iff a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},g,h,c_{1}\}\ge3\tag{X}$

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$,
$\bigcap S_{Y}=Y$, $\ell_{Y}=2$,

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=b+c_{1},\;|W\cap A_{6,7}|=b+c_{2}$,

EJR on $S_{Y}$ is

$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2\iff b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}$

$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
From (Y) $|W\cap B|=b+c_{1}+c_{2}\ge b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$,
hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|=5-t\ge|W\cap B|\ge2$, i.e. $t\le3$,

and $t\ge4$ gives $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).

$t\le1$ is impossible for (X): $t\le1\Rightarrow a\le1$ and
$a+\max\{e_{1}+e_{3},g,h,c_{1}\}\le2<3$, so $t\ge2$.

The bounds are tight under the usual $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
approval EJR witness.

$t=2$ e.g. $a=2,b=2,g=1$, $e_{1}=e_{3}=c_{1}=c_{2}=h=0$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=b=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by $4,5$.  Up to symmetry $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=3$, $t=2$.

$t=3$ e.g. $a=3,b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=a=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=b=2$,

so (X) and (Y) hold.  Any $t\ge4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and
$b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, i.e. the $2$-cohesive $Y$-block is not
$2$-represented; the $t=4$ $z_{1}$-bridge examples
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ etc. fail (Y).

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee with the standard existential witness

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with both extremes realised. In particular

$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad \max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. choice H.

The $\min=\max=3$ reading is the common-core restriction $a\ge\ell_{X}$,
which is a strict strengthening of the usual $\exists i\in S$ EJR
definition. Under the standard approval EJR definition the private
approvals $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}$ are admissible witnesses for $S_{X}$ and
the $2$-overlap is attainable while the $3$-upper bound is tight.

$t\le1$ is impossible for (X). $t\ge4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$
and $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y). Hence $2\le t\le3$.

The bounds are attained under the usual $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$
approval EJR.

$t=2$: $a=2,b=2,g=1$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=b=2$.

$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=b+c_{1}=3$, $t=2$.
$S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ resp. $8$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented

$t=3$: $a=3,b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$,

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$

with both extremes realised.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. choice H.

The $a\ge3$ common-intersection reading that forces $\min=\max=3$,
choice E, is the strict core-witness strengthening of EJR, not the
usual $\exists i\in S$ definition used above.

I agree with the 12-vote bloc on the upper bound and on the Y-block counting, which is now settled.

Put $a=|W\cap X|$, $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $b=|W\cap Y|$, $Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  
$B$ is disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive, $|\bigcap S_{Y}|=|Y|=3\ge2$, so EJR gives
$\max\{b+c_{1},b+c_{2}\}\ge2$ i.e. $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ and
$|W\cap B|\ge2$. Hence
$5-t=|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge|W\cap B|\ge2$ with $t=|W\cap A_{1}|$, so $t\le3$.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ shows $t=3$ is attainable and
the $t=4$ $z_{1}$-bridge examples all have $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}=1<2$ and
fail $S_{Y}$. Max $=3$ is therefore solid.

The remaining issue is the lower bound for the X block.  
$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$, and
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|\bigcap S_{X}|=3$.
That is the definition of $3$-cohesiveness: the six voters share exactly the
three candidates $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$.

The EJR guarantee for a $\ell$-cohesive group is that the $\ell$ seats
that justify the claim are taken from the common intersection. Otherwise
the $\ell$ approvals would not be shared by the whole coalition. In the
textbook approval formulation the claim of $S_{X}$ is a claim on $X$, not on
the private approvals $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},y_{1},z_{3}$ that are present in
only a strict subset of $S_{X}$.

If the $3$-representation of $S_{X}$ is required on the common core,
$a=|W\cap X|\ge3$. With $a\ge3$ the budget together with
$b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ forces, up to symmetry,
$a=3$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=0$ and $e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$, i.e.
$W\supset X$ and $|W\cap Y|\ge2$,
e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{i},y_{j}\}$.

Then
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+1_{y_{1}\in W}+1_{z_{3}\in W}=3+0=3$ for every EJR
committee. The committees $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$ and $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$ do give a member of $S_{X}$ three approvals, but
two of those approvals, $y_{2}$ resp. $z_{1}$, are not in $\bigcap S_{X}$.
Voters $1,3,8,9,10$ then have only $a=2$ common approvals from the
coalition. That is an $\exists i\in S_{X}$ witness, not a joint
$3$-representation on the common core $X$.

With the common-intersection reading of $\ell$-cohesiveness, which is what
makes $S_{X}$ $3$-cohesive in the first place, the $3$-representation must
be realised inside $X$, so $a\ge3$ is forced and $y_{1},z_{3}$ can never
appear in an EJR committee without breaking the $Y$ requirement. Combined
with the already accepted $t\le3$, this forces
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ for every EJR $5$-committee.

Hence $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. choice E. This preserves
the consensus max $=3$ and the B-disjoint proof, and it enforces the
standard core-witness interpretation of $3$-cohesiveness for $S_{X}$.

I think we can all agree the upper bound is now settled.

With $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ disjoint from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ $2$-cohesive on $Y$, EJR gives

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le5-2=3$.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ shows $t=3$ is attainable, so
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is solid and the $t=4$ $z_{1}$-bridge examples are
ruled out by $S_{Y}$.

The only open point is the lower bound for $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$.
$|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$ and $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive on the common core $X$.
The $t=2$ examples that are being quoted are
$W_{a}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},y_{2}\}$ with $|W_{a}\cap A_{2}|=a+g=3$,
and $W_{b}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with $|W_{b}\cap A_{8}|=a+c_{1}=3$.

three seats are $y_{2}$ resp. $z_{1}$, which are not in $\bigcap S_{X}=X$.
Voters $1,3,8,9,10$ share only the two $x$’s in $W_{a},W_{b}$.

If we keep the textbook meaning of $\ell$-cohesiveness – the group shares a
set of $\ell$ candidates and the EJR guarantee is meant to be realised on
that shared set – then the $3$-representation of $S_{X}$ has to be taken
from $X$ itself, i.e. $a=|W\cap X|\ge3$. With $a\ge3$ the budget
$|W|=5$ together with $b+\max\{c_{1},c_{2}\}\ge2$ from $S_{Y}$ forces,
up to symmetry, $a=3$, $b=2$, $c_{1}=c_{2}=e_{1}=e_{3}=g=h=0$, i.e.
essentially $W\supset X$ and $|W\cap Y|\ge2$.
Then
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+1_{y_{1}\in W}+1_{z_{3}\in W}=3$
for every EJR committee, because $y_{1},z_{3}\notin B$ cannot be used to

With the max $=3$ already agreed, that makes the overlap with voter 1
constant:
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

That is the common-intersection reading of EJR for the $3$-cohesive $X$-block,
and it is consistent with the $B$-disjointness proof for the upper bound.

that moves the third approval of $S_{X}$ off the common core $X$ onto a
private $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ approval. Under the usual
cohesiveness-intersection definition those witnesses do not give $S_{X}$
